note: Commerce round 3 (part B): insurance, banking, the stock exchange, business units, sources of business finance, business management, marketing, advertising, consumer protection, trade associations, government and business - scenario items with a fire-insurance case passage and a company capital-structure table.

passages.title: Fire at Okonkwo Stores
passages.text: Mr Okonkwo owns a provisions store valued at ₦50 million. He insured it against fire with Crest Insurance for ₦40 million at an annual premium of 1% of the sum insured. On 2 April a fire destroyed goods and fittings worth ₦10 million. The policy contains an average clause. When investigating the claim, Crest Insurance discovered that Mr Okonkwo had truthfully declared, when applying, that a kerosene depot operates next door.

passages.title: Capital structure of Delta Foods Plc
passages.text:
Delta Foods Plc has the following capital.

Item                       ₦ million
Ordinary shares of ₦1 each       200
8% preference shares of ₦1        50
10% debentures                   100
Retained profits                  30

In 2025 the company made a profit of
₦34 million before paying debenture
interest and any dividend.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The annual premium Mr Okonkwo pays to Crest Insurance is
questions.explanation: Premium = 1% of the sum insured of ₦40 million = ₦400,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Applying the average clause, Crest Insurance will pay Mr Okonkwo
questions.explanation: Under average the insurer pays loss × (sum insured ÷ value) = ₦10m × 40/50 = ₦8 million; the owner bears the rest because he under-insured.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Okonkwo bears part of the loss himself because
questions.A: fire policies never pay the full loss
questions.B: the fire was caused by the kerosene depot
questions.D: he insured the store for less than its full value
questions.explanation: The average clause penalises under-insurance in proportion to the shortfall.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Okonkwo's declaration about the kerosene depot satisfied the insurance principle of
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) requires the proposer to disclose all material facts; a nearby kerosene depot raises the risk of fire.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: If Mr Okonkwo had concealed the existence of the kerosene depot, Crest Insurance could have
questions.A: been forced by law to pay the full ₦50 million
questions.B: paid double the claim as a penalty on itself
questions.C: refused to pay the claim because a material fact was not disclosed
questions.D: transferred the policy to the kerosene depot owner
questions.explanation: Non-disclosure of a material fact entitles the insurer to avoid the contract.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The insurable interest that allowed Mr Okonkwo to take out the policy arises from the fact that he
questions.A: pays tax to the local government in whose area the store stands
questions.B: lives in the same street as the store and passes it every day
questions.C: has been a customer of Crest Insurance for more than ten years
questions.D: owns the store and would suffer financially if it were destroyed
questions.explanation: Insurable interest exists when the insured stands to lose financially from the event insured against.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: After paying the claim, Crest Insurance learns that the fire was caused by the negligence of the kerosene depot and sues the depot to recover what it paid. This illustrates
questions.explanation: By subrogation the insurer, having indemnified the insured, steps into his shoes to pursue the third party responsible.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The annual interest Delta Foods Plc must pay on its debentures is
questions.explanation: 10% of ₦100 million = ₦10 million, payable whether or not the company makes a profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The dividend due to the preference shareholders for 2025 is
questions.explanation: 8% of ₦50 million = ₦4 million, paid after debenture interest but before any ordinary dividend.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: If the directors distribute all the profit remaining after debenture interest and the preference dividend, the ordinary dividend per share is
questions.explanation: ₦34m − ₦10m interest − ₦4m preference dividend = ₦20m for 200 million ordinary shares = ₦0.10 (10 kobo) per share.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The item in the capital structure that represents borrowed money rather than ownership is
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are creditors who receive interest; shareholders are owners who receive dividends.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: If Delta Foods Plc made no profit at all in 2026, it would still be legally obliged to pay
questions.C: an ordinary dividend of 10 kobo per share
questions.explanation: Interest on debentures is a debt due whether or not profits are made; dividends are paid only out of profits.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The retained profits of ₦30 million represent
questions.A: money borrowed from the bank on overdraft to finance daily trading
questions.B: profits ploughed back into the business instead of being distributed
questions.C: the amount owed to trade creditors for goods supplied on credit
questions.D: the market value of the company's shares on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Retained (undistributed) profits are an internal source of finance belonging to the ordinary shareholders.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Audu insured his goods in transit for ₦2 million. The goods were destroyed in an accident and he claimed ₦2 million from each of the two companies with which he had insured them. Under the principle of contribution he will
questions.A: receive nothing, because double insurance is illegal
questions.B: receive ₦4 million, ₦2 million from each insurer
questions.C: receive ₦2 million in total, shared between the two insurers
questions.D: receive ₦2 million from each insurer plus interest
questions.explanation: Contribution prevents profit from double insurance; the insurers share the one indemnity between them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cargo ship sank after its cargo had been damaged by seawater following a collision. The loss that the marine insurer will consider is determined by the principle of
questions.explanation: Proximate cause identifies the dominant, effective cause of the loss to decide whether it is an insured peril.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following risks cannot be insured?
questions.A: damage to a shop and its stock caused by fire
questions.B: loss arising from a fall in demand for a product
questions.C: theft of goods from a warehouse by burglars
questions.D: injury to a worker while operating a machine
questions.explanation: Business (speculative) risks such as falling demand or bad management cannot be measured or insured against.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The premium charged by an insurer is fixed mainly on the basis of
questions.A: the age of the insurance company
questions.C: the degree of risk and the sum insured
questions.D: the number of employees of the insurer
questions.explanation: Higher risk (e.g. a timber store) and a higher sum insured mean a higher premium.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Insurance works on the principle of pooling of risks, which means that
questions.A: the government pays all insurance claims
questions.B: every insured person receives a claim each year
questions.C: the insurer bears all losses from its own profits
questions.D: the premiums of the many pay for the losses of the few
questions.explanation: Many people contribute premiums into a pool from which those who suffer loss are compensated.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A motorist insures only against liability for injury to other people and damage to their property. This cover is
questions.explanation: Third-party insurance, compulsory in Nigeria, covers liability to others but not the insured's own vehicle.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A comprehensive motor policy differs from a third-party policy in that it also covers
questions.B: injuries to other road users only
questions.C: damage to or loss of the insured's own vehicle
questions.explanation: Comprehensive cover adds own-damage, fire and theft of the insured vehicle to third-party liability.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bank insures itself against losses caused by dishonesty of its cashiers. This is
questions.explanation: Fidelity guarantee protects an employer against fraud or embezzlement by employees.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: After a fire, a factory could not produce for three months and lost profits. The policy that compensates for such lost profits is
questions.explanation: Consequential (loss of profits) insurance covers the income lost while the business is interrupted.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mrs Bello takes a policy that pays ₦5 million to her family if she dies within 20 years, but pays nothing if she survives the period. This is
questions.explanation: Term assurance covers death within a fixed period only; it is cheap because there may be no payout.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A policy that pays a lump sum either on the death of the assured or at the end of a fixed period, whichever comes first, is
questions.explanation: Endowment combines protection with saving; it matures at a fixed date if the assured is still alive.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Okafor's fire insurer paid only the actual value of his burnt goods, but on his death his family received the full ₦10 million on his life policy even though he had paid only two premiums. The difference arises because
questions.A: fire insurance companies are permitted by law to pay less than they owe
questions.B: life assurance is not a contract of indemnity, since a life cannot be valued in money
questions.C: life policies pay only if the assured has paid premiums for at least ten years
questions.D: fire policies pay in full only when the insured has died in the fire
questions.explanation: Indemnity applies to property insurance; a life policy pays the agreed sum because human life cannot be valued in money.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An insurer that passes part of a very large risk to another insurer is engaged in
questions.explanation: Re-insurance spreads a big risk (e.g. an oil refinery) so that no single insurer bears it all.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The insurance term 'the insured' refers to
questions.A: the government body that regulates insurance companies
questions.B: the company that issues the policy and collects the premium
questions.C: the agent who sells the policy on commission
questions.D: the person or firm that takes out the policy and is protected by it
questions.explanation: The insured (or assured) is protected; the insurer provides the cover.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A document containing the terms of an insurance contract is
questions.explanation: The policy is the formal contract; the proposal form is the application and the cover note gives temporary cover.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Chukwu applied for motor insurance and paid the premium, but the policy has not yet been prepared. To drive legally in the meantime he should hold
questions.explanation: The cover note gives temporary evidence of insurance until the policy and certificate are issued.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The regulatory body for insurance business in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NAICOM licenses and supervises insurers, brokers and agents.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An insurance broker differs from an insurance agent in that a broker
questions.A: is employed by one insurer to sell that insurer's policies only
questions.B: is an independent professional acting for the insured, dealing with many insurers
questions.C: pays claims to policy holders out of his own funds
questions.D: issues policies in his own name
questions.explanation: Brokers advise clients and place their business with any suitable insurer; agents represent a particular insurer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader insured goods worth ₦5 million for ₦5 million. Fire damaged goods worth ₦1.5 million, and he had already sold the damaged remains for ₦300,000. Under indemnity the insurer pays
questions.explanation: Indemnity restores the insured to his position before the loss: ₦1.5m loss less ₦300,000 salvage = ₦1.2 million.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Marine insurance covers
questions.A: buildings near the sea against burglary and housebreaking
questions.B: only the lives of sailors and fishermen while they are at sea
questions.C: goods carried by road and rail from one town to another
questions.D: ships, their cargo and freight against the perils of the sea
questions.explanation: Hull, cargo and freight policies protect against sea perils such as sinking, fire and collision.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Insurance benefits commerce by
questions.A: guaranteeing that no loss will ever occur to an insured business
questions.B: enabling traders to undertake risky ventures with confidence and providing funds for investment
questions.C: removing the need for banks and other financial institutions
questions.D: compelling every trader to pay higher prices for his goods
questions.explanation: Insurance spreads risk and insurers invest pooled premiums, which also provides capital to the economy.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An annuity is an arrangement under which
questions.A: an insurer pays for damage caused by floods to houses built near a river
questions.B: a business pays a yearly premium and its stock is insured against fire and theft
questions.C: a person pays a lump sum and receives a regular income for life or a fixed period
questions.D: a motorist is compensated for a car stolen from outside his house at night
questions.explanation: Annuities are used to provide retirement income.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The main reason why the law makes third-party motor insurance compulsory is to
questions.A: ensure that every motorist buys a new car
questions.B: increase the revenue of insurance companies
questions.C: reduce the number of vehicles on the road
questions.D: ensure that victims of road accidents can be compensated
questions.explanation: Compulsory third-party cover guarantees a source of compensation for people injured by insured drivers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mrs Okoye keeps money in an account from which she can withdraw at any time by cheque and on which the bank pays little or no interest. The account is
questions.explanation: Current accounts provide cheque facilities and are used for business payments.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader deposits ₦5 million with a bank for 180 days at an agreed interest rate and cannot withdraw it before then without losing interest. This is
questions.explanation: Fixed deposits earn higher interest because the money is committed for a stated period.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cheque that is more than six months old and which a bank refuses to pay is
questions.explanation: Banks treat cheques presented more than six months after their date as stale.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cheque dated 1 December 2026 presented for payment on 15 September 2026 is
questions.explanation: A post-dated cheque bears a future date and is not payable until that date.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cheque crossed 'Account payee only' can be paid
questions.A: into the account of anyone the payee endorses it to
questions.B: over the counter to any person who presents it
questions.C: only into the bank account of the named payee
questions.D: only at the branch where the drawer keeps his account
questions.explanation: The crossing restricts payment to the payee's own account, making the cheque safe if lost or stolen.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In a cheque transaction, the person who writes and signs the cheque is
questions.explanation: The drawer signs; the drawee is the bank on which it is drawn; the payee receives the money.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The bank on which a cheque is drawn is called
questions.explanation: The drawee bank pays the cheque out of the drawer's account.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bank returned a cheque marked 'words and figures differ'. The error was that
questions.A: the cheque was presented more than six months after its date
questions.B: the drawer had no money in the account on which the cheque was drawn
questions.C: the amount written in words did not agree with the amount in figures
questions.D: the name of the payee was not written on the face of the cheque
questions.explanation: Banks dishonour cheques on which the amount in words and figures do not match.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader who needs to pay ₦3 million to a supplier in another state without carrying cash and without the supplier fearing a bounced cheque should use
questions.explanation: A bank draft is drawn by the bank on itself, so payment is guaranteed.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a function of a commercial bank?
questions.C: acting as lender of last resort
questions.explanation: Commercial banks take deposits, lend, and provide payment services; the others are central bank functions.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Many depositors rushed to withdraw their money from Zenith Trust Bank on the same day and the bank ran short of cash. The institution that would lend to the bank to meet the withdrawals is
questions.A: the Corporate Affairs Commission, acting as registrar
questions.B: the Nigerian Exchange, acting as market maker
questions.C: the Central Bank of Nigeria, acting as lender of last resort
questions.D: the National Insurance Commission, acting as guarantor
questions.explanation: The central bank supports the banking system by lending to banks in temporary difficulty.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: When the Central Bank raises the cash reserve ratio, commercial banks
questions.A: are allowed to print more naira notes
questions.B: have more money available to lend
questions.C: must close some of their branches
questions.D: have less money available to lend
questions.explanation: A higher reserve ratio forces banks to keep more of their deposits idle at the central bank, reducing credit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bank customer with ₦100,000 in his current account pays a cheque for ₦150,000 which the bank honours under an agreed facility. The bank has granted
questions.explanation: An overdraft allows a customer to draw more than the balance in his current account up to an agreed limit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An automated teller machine (ATM) allows a customer to
questions.A: buy shares on the stock exchange
questions.B: obtain a loan without any documentation
questions.C: withdraw cash and check balances without a cashier
questions.explanation: ATMs provide 24-hour access to cash and simple account services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A merchant bank differs from a commercial bank in that a merchant bank
questions.A: operates only in rural areas where there are no other banks
questions.B: accepts small savings deposits from members of the general public
questions.C: issues the currency notes and coins used throughout the country
questions.D: specialises in wholesale banking, corporate finance and accepting bills
questions.explanation: Merchant (investment) banks serve companies with large loans, share issues and trade finance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The clearing house is the place where
questions.B: banks settle cheques drawn on one another
questions.C: the central bank prints new notes
questions.D: foreign currencies are sold to travellers
questions.explanation: Cheques drawn on other banks are exchanged and net balances settled through the clearing system.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A direct debit differs from a standing order in that under a direct debit
questions.A: the customer must sign a cheque for every payment
questions.B: the bank pays a fixed amount on a fixed date each month
questions.C: the payee collects varying amounts as they fall due, with the customer's authority
questions.D: payment can be made in cash only
questions.explanation: Standing orders pay fixed regular sums; direct debits let the creditor claim amounts that may vary, such as electricity bills.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mobile money and USSD banking have helped commerce in Nigeria mainly by
questions.A: guaranteeing profit to every trader who uses them
questions.B: abolishing the use of cash in all transactions
questions.C: removing the need for the Central Bank
questions.D: allowing people without bank branches nearby to send and receive payments
questions.explanation: Payments by phone extend financial services to rural and unbanked areas.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Sani borrowed ₦800,000 from a bank at 15% per annum simple interest for 3 years. The total interest he pays is
questions.explanation: Simple interest = principal × rate × time = ₦800,000 × 0.15 × 3 = ₦360,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader deposited ₦1,000,000 at 10% per annum compound interest for 2 years. The amount at the end of the period is

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following documents is used to pay money into a bank account?
questions.explanation: The teller or pay-in slip records the cash or cheques deposited.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bank statement is
questions.A: an order by a customer to his bank to pay a fixed sum every month
questions.B: a record sent by the bank showing the transactions on a customer's account
questions.C: a document a customer completes when withdrawing cash over the counter
questions.D: a certificate issued by the bank when a fixed deposit is opened
questions.explanation: The statement lists deposits, withdrawals, charges and the running balance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Before granting a loan, a bank asks a trader for collateral security. The purpose is to
questions.A: prevent the trader from opening another account
questions.B: increase the amount of interest payable
questions.C: give the bank something to sell if the loan is not repaid
questions.explanation: Collateral (land, buildings, shares) protects the bank against default.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bank endorses a customer's bill of exchange, guaranteeing payment. The bank has
questions.explanation: By accepting (endorsing) a bill, the bank undertakes to pay if the drawee fails.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader holding a ₦500,000 bill of exchange due in 90 days needs cash now. He can obtain it by
questions.A: crossing the bill 'account payee' and paying it into his account
questions.B: discounting the bill with his bank for less than its face value
questions.C: waiting until the bill matures and then presenting it for payment
questions.D: returning the bill to the drawee and asking for a fresh one
questions.explanation: Discounting means selling the bill before maturity; the bank deducts interest (discount) for the period.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a service rendered by commercial banks?
questions.explanation: Only the Central Bank issues currency.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Bank Verification Number (BVN) was introduced in Nigeria mainly to
questions.A: allow customers to borrow without collateral
questions.B: increase the interest paid on deposits
questions.C: replace the naira with a digital currency
questions.D: identify each bank customer uniquely and reduce fraud
questions.explanation: The BVN links a customer's biometric data to all his accounts, curbing identity fraud.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Development banks such as the Bank of Industry differ from commercial banks in that they
questions.A: accept small deposits from the general public and pay interest on them
questions.B: give medium- and long-term loans to promote development in particular sectors
questions.C: print and issue the national currency on behalf of the government
questions.D: operate only at the seaports and airports to serve importers
questions.explanation: Development banks finance industry, agriculture and infrastructure over long periods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A letter of credit is useful in foreign trade because it
questions.A: allows the goods to be shipped without any documents being prepared at all
questions.B: exempts the importer from paying customs duty on the goods when they arrive
questions.C: assures the exporter that a bank will pay once the shipping documents are presented
questions.D: fixes the rate of exchange between the two currencies for a whole year
questions.explanation: The importer's bank undertakes to pay the exporter against documents, removing the risk of non-payment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An endorsement on a cheque is
questions.A: the date on which the cheque becomes stale
questions.B: the bank's stamp showing that the cheque has bounced
questions.C: a note written by the drawer cancelling the cheque
questions.D: the payee's signature on the back transferring the cheque to another person
questions.explanation: Order cheques are negotiated by endorsement; bearer cheques need none.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The market in which existing shares are bought and sold is
questions.explanation: New issues are sold in the primary market; the stock exchange provides a secondary market for existing securities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company raising money by issuing new shares to the public for the first time is making
questions.explanation: An IPO is the first sale of a company's shares to the public, after which they are listed on the exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company gives its shareholders one free share for every five held, capitalising its reserves. This is
questions.explanation: Bonus shares are issued free out of reserves; rights issues are offered for cash at a discount.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An investor who expects share prices to fall and sells now hoping to buy back cheaply is called
questions.explanation: Bears sell in expectation of a fall; bulls buy expecting a rise; stags apply for new issues to sell at a quick profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A person who applies for new shares in a public offer intending to sell them quickly at a premium is
questions.explanation: Stags profit from the price rise that often follows a popular new issue.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A member of the public wishing to buy shares on the Nigerian Exchange must go through
questions.explanation: Only licensed stockbrokers deal on the exchange on behalf of clients.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The body that regulates the Nigerian capital market and protects investors is
questions.explanation: SEC registers securities, licenses operators and supervises the Nigerian Exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Ordinary shareholders differ from preference shareholders in that ordinary shareholders
questions.B: receive a fixed dividend before others
questions.C: receive a dividend that varies with profits and have voting rights
questions.D: are paid interest whether or not profits are made
questions.explanation: Ordinary shares carry the risk and the votes; preference shares get a fixed dividend first but usually no vote.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Cumulative preference shares entitle their holders to
questions.A: receive a share of the profits in addition to the fixed dividend
questions.B: convert their shares into debentures at any time
questions.C: vote at every general meeting of the company
questions.D: receive arrears of unpaid dividend from earlier years before ordinary shareholders are paid
questions.explanation: If a dividend is missed in a bad year, it accumulates and must be paid later before any ordinary dividend.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mr Eze lent ₦2 million to Sunrise Plc by buying its 12% debentures. In relation to the company, Mr Eze is
questions.A: an owner who receives a variable dividend
questions.B: a creditor who receives a fixed rate of interest
questions.C: a member with voting rights at general meetings
questions.D: a director responsible for its management
questions.explanation: Debentures are loan capital; interest is payable whether or not the company makes profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The main advantage of listing a company's shares on the stock exchange is that
questions.A: the company's shares can never fall in value
questions.B: the company no longer needs to publish accounts
questions.C: shareholders can easily sell their shares, which encourages investment
questions.D: the directors are exempted from paying tax
questions.explanation: The exchange provides liquidity; investors are more willing to buy shares they can sell readily.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Government securities such as treasury bills and FGN bonds are considered safe because
questions.A: they are issued only to banks
questions.B: they pay the highest interest in the market
questions.C: they can never be sold before maturity
questions.D: the government is very unlikely to default on payment
questions.explanation: Gilt-edged securities are backed by the government's power to tax.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A treasury bill differs from an FGN bond in that a treasury bill
questions.A: pays a higher fixed interest for 20 years
questions.B: is a short-term security, usually maturing within a year
questions.D: gives the holder a share in government profits
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are 91-, 182- or 364-day instruments; bonds run for several years.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Shares bought at ₦20 each now sell at ₦26. A shareholder who sells 2,000 shares makes a capital gain of

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company's shares have a nominal (par) value of 50 kobo but sell on the exchange at ₦8. The ₦8 is
questions.explanation: Market value is set by demand and supply on the exchange; nominal value is the face value printed on the share.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A share with a market price of ₦40 pays a dividend of ₦3.20. Its dividend yield is
questions.explanation: Yield = dividend ÷ market price × 100 = 3.20 ÷ 40 × 100 = 8%.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The All-Share Index of the Nigerian Exchange measures
questions.A: the total number of companies in Nigeria
questions.C: the general movement of share prices on the exchange
questions.D: the exchange rate of the naira
questions.explanation: A rising index shows that share prices are generally increasing.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The stock exchange helps the economy by
questions.A: insuring investors against any loss they may suffer on their shares
questions.B: printing money for the government whenever it needs to pay its workers
questions.C: fixing the prices at which consumer goods are sold in the markets
questions.D: channelling savings into long-term investment in companies and government projects
questions.explanation: The capital market mobilises savings and allocates them to productive uses.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A unit trust (mutual fund) is a scheme in which
questions.A: a single wealthy investor buys all the shares of one company and manages it himself
questions.B: many small investors pool money that professional managers invest in a spread of securities
questions.C: the government sells treasury bills to the commercial banks at a discount
questions.D: commercial banks lend money to stockbrokers to buy shares for their clients
questions.explanation: Unit trusts give small savers diversification and expert management.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company declares a dividend of 15 kobo per share. An investor holding 40,000 shares receives
questions.explanation: Dividend received = number of shares × dividend per share = 40,000 × ₦0.15 = ₦6,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Speculation on the stock exchange means
questions.B: holding shares for many years to receive dividends
questions.C: lending money to the government at a fixed rate
questions.D: buying or selling securities in the hope of profiting from price changes
questions.explanation: Speculators trade on expected price movements rather than for long-term income.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Securities that a company issues and can later convert into ordinary shares at the holder's option are
questions.explanation: Convertible loan stock gives lenders the chance to become shareholders if the company prospers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Chinedu opened a barbing salon with his savings, makes all decisions himself and keeps all the profit. His business is
questions.explanation: One owner, unlimited liability, total control and all the profit describe a sole trader.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A major disadvantage of the sole proprietorship is that
questions.A: the business must publish its accounts every year
questions.B: profits must be shared with many partners
questions.C: decisions take a long time because many people must agree
questions.D: the owner's personal property can be seized to pay business debts
questions.explanation: Unlimited liability means there is no legal separation between the owner and the business.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A partner who contributes capital and shares profits but takes no part in running the business and is not known to the public is
questions.explanation: Sleeping partners invest but do not manage; nominal partners lend their name without capital.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A partnership between two doctors ends automatically when
questions.A: one partner goes on annual leave
questions.B: the partnership makes a loss in one year
questions.C: one partner dies or becomes bankrupt
questions.D: the partnership employs a new nurse
questions.explanation: Death, bankruptcy or insanity of a partner dissolves the partnership unless the deed provides otherwise.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The document that sets out how partners will share profits, contribute capital and settle disputes is
questions.explanation: The deed governs the relationship between partners; without one the Partnership Act applies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, profits are shared
questions.C: according to the age of the partners
questions.D: as decided by the eldest partner
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership Act, partners share profits and losses equally where there is no agreement.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A limited partner is one whose liability for the firm's debts
questions.A: is borne entirely by the other partners in the firm
questions.B: extends to all his personal property and future income
questions.C: is restricted to the capital he has agreed to contribute
questions.D: is guaranteed by the government up to a fixed amount
questions.explanation: Limited partners enjoy limited liability but may not take part in management; at least one partner must have unlimited liability.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The maximum number of partners permitted in an ordinary partnership under Nigerian law is
questions.explanation: Ordinary partnerships are limited to 20 members (professional firms such as lawyers and accountants may exceed this).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Six friends want to start a business in which their personal property will be safe if the business fails and they do not intend to sell shares to the public. The most suitable form is
questions.explanation: A private company (Ltd) gives limited liability and restricts share transfers; a Plc offers shares to the public.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The document that regulates the internal management of a company, such as the powers of directors and the conduct of meetings, is
questions.explanation: The memorandum governs the company's relations with outsiders; the articles govern internal affairs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company becomes a legal person separate from its owners when it receives
questions.explanation: Incorporation creates the company as a separate legal entity that can sue, be sued and own property.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A public limited company may not begin business until it obtains, in addition to the certificate of incorporation,
questions.A: a partnership deed signed by all the directors
questions.B: a certificate of trading (commencement of business)
questions.C: an import licence issued by the customs service
questions.D: a listing on the floor of the stock exchange
questions.explanation: A Plc needs the certificate of trading confirming that the minimum capital has been raised.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A document inviting the public to subscribe for a company's shares is
questions.explanation: The prospectus gives information about the company so that investors can decide whether to buy.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of a public limited company over a partnership?
questions.A: decisions are taken quickly by one person
questions.B: its affairs are kept private from the public
questions.C: it is easy and cheap to form
questions.D: it can raise large capital by selling shares to the public
questions.explanation: Access to public capital and limited liability are the main strengths of the Plc.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A disadvantage of the public limited company is that
questions.A: the owners have unlimited liability and may lose their personal property for its debts
questions.B: ownership is separated from control, and shareholders have little say in daily management
questions.C: it cannot raise more than ₦1 million in capital from the public at any one time
questions.D: it must be dissolved and re-registered whenever one of its shareholders dies
questions.explanation: Shareholders own but directors and managers control; the Plc also faces heavy regulation and disclosure.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A limited liability company's debts of ₦50 million exceed its assets of ₦30 million. A shareholder who has fully paid for ₦100,000 of shares
questions.A: must sell his house to pay the creditors
questions.B: must contribute to the ₦20 million shortfall
questions.D: is entitled to a refund of his ₦100,000
questions.explanation: Limited liability caps a shareholder's loss at the amount unpaid (if any) on his shares.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A public corporation such as the Nigerian Ports Authority is
questions.A: a partnership between the government and foreign firms
questions.B: owned by shareholders who bought shares on the stock exchange
questions.C: owned by its workers as a cooperative
questions.D: owned by the government and set up by an Act of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: Public corporations are statutory bodies owned by the state to provide essential services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A reason for establishing public corporations is to
questions.A: guarantee a high rate of profit for private shareholders every year
questions.B: provide essential services that private investors may find unprofitable
questions.C: reduce the number of civil servants employed by the government
questions.D: avoid the need for the government to prepare an annual budget
questions.explanation: Public corporations provide utilities, ports and other essential services and prevent private monopoly abuse.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The sale of government-owned enterprises to private investors is called
questions.explanation: Privatisation transfers ownership from the state to private hands; nationalisation is the reverse.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cooperative society differs from a public limited company in that in a cooperative
questions.A: profits are never distributed to members
questions.B: voting rights depend on the number of shares held
questions.D: each member has one vote regardless of the number of shares held
questions.explanation: Cooperatives are democratic: one member, one vote; companies vote by shares.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Farmers who form a society to buy seeds and fertiliser in bulk and market their crops together have formed
questions.explanation: Producer cooperatives help members buy inputs and sell output on better terms.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A thrift and credit cooperative society helps its members mainly by
questions.A: employing them in a factory owned by the society
questions.B: selling consumer goods to them at prices above the market
questions.C: pooling their savings and granting them loans at low interest
questions.D: paying their income tax to the government each year
questions.explanation: Thrift and credit (savings and loan) societies provide cheap credit from members' pooled savings.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company that owns more than 50% of the shares of another company is called
questions.explanation: The controlled company is the subsidiary; the controller is the holding (parent) company.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Two soap manufacturers combine to form a single larger company. This is
questions.explanation: A merger unites two companies into one; a cartel is an agreement between firms that remain separate.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A textile firm buys the cotton ginnery that supplies it. This is
questions.explanation: Buying a supplier is backward integration; buying a customer (e.g. a retail chain) is forward integration.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The annual general meeting (AGM) of a company is attended by
questions.A: the government officials who regulate the company
questions.D: the shareholders, who elect directors and receive the accounts
questions.explanation: At the AGM shareholders exercise their ownership rights: electing directors, approving dividends and appointing auditors.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Indigenisation, as applied in Nigeria in the 1970s, meant
questions.A: selling government-owned companies to foreign investors
questions.B: transferring ownership of certain foreign businesses to Nigerians
questions.C: banning all foreign investment in the Nigerian economy
questions.D: merging all private companies into a single state company
questions.explanation: The indigenisation decrees reserved specified enterprises wholly or partly for Nigerian ownership.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The cheapest source of finance for a sole trader who wants to expand is usually
questions.C: his own savings and ploughed-back profit
questions.explanation: Retained profit and personal savings carry no interest or issue costs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader who needs money for three weeks to buy stock for the Christmas season should seek
questions.explanation: Overdrafts are flexible short-term finance; interest is paid only on the amount and time used.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company borrows ₦200 million for ten years secured on its factory buildings. This source of finance is
questions.explanation: A mortgage is long-term borrowing secured on landed property.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A firm sells its debtors' invoices to a finance house at a discount and receives cash immediately. This is
questions.explanation: Factoring turns trade debts into immediate cash; the factor collects from the debtors.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a short-term source of finance?
questions.explanation: Trade credit, overdrafts and short-term loans finance day-to-day needs; shares and debentures are long-term.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The main difference between a share and a debenture as sources of finance is that
questions.A: a debenture gives voting rights while a share does not
questions.B: a share gives ownership while a debenture is a loan
questions.C: a share must be repaid at a fixed date while a debenture is permanent
questions.D: a debenture receives dividends while a share receives interest
questions.explanation: Shareholders are owners paid dividends; debenture holders are creditors paid interest.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company that raises additional capital by offering new shares to its existing shareholders at a price below the market price is making
questions.explanation: Rights issues raise cash from existing members in proportion to their holdings.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bus company acquires new buses under an agreement to pay a deposit and monthly instalments, becoming the owner after the last payment. This is
questions.explanation: Ownership passes on the final instalment under hire purchase; under a lease it never passes.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Leasing equipment rather than buying it benefits a small firm because
questions.A: it becomes the owner of the equipment at once
questions.B: it can use the equipment without tying up capital in purchase
questions.C: the lessor pays for the firm's raw materials
questions.D: it never has to pay anything for the equipment
questions.explanation: Leasing spreads the cost as rentals and keeps capital free for working needs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an internal source of finance for a company?
questions.explanation: Internal finance comes from within the business: retained profits and sale of surplus assets.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cooperative society usually obtains its capital from
questions.explanation: Cooperatives are financed mainly by their members' contributions and loans from cooperative banks.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Bank of Agriculture and the Bank of Industry are important sources of finance because they
questions.A: accept current account deposits from traders and pay interest on the balances
questions.B: provide medium- and long-term loans at concessionary rates to farmers and manufacturers
questions.C: sell the shares of foreign companies to Nigerians who want to invest abroad
questions.D: issue treasury bills and bonds to the public on behalf of the federal government
questions.explanation: Development finance institutions lend on softer terms than commercial banks to promote key sectors.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Venture capital is
questions.A: money that a trader keeps in a savings account for use in an emergency
questions.B: a short-term loan from a bank for buying stock before a festive season
questions.C: money invested in a new or risky business in return for a share of ownership
questions.D: credit given by a supplier to a retailer for a period of thirty days
questions.explanation: Venture capitalists take equity stakes in promising young firms that banks consider too risky.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Government grants to small businesses differ from loans in that grants
questions.A: are secured on the owner's house
questions.B: carry a higher rate of interest
questions.C: must be repaid within one year
questions.D: do not have to be repaid
questions.explanation: A grant is a gift for a stated purpose; a loan must be repaid with interest.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer buys goods worth ₦1,000,000 on terms '2/10, net 30'. If he pays within 10 days he saves
questions.explanation: 2% cash discount for payment within 10 days = ₦20,000; otherwise the full ₦1,000,000 is due in 30 days.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Sources of finance available to a partnership include all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Only companies can issue shares; partnerships rely on partners' funds, loans and credit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A managing director decides that the company will open ten new branches in the next five years. This management function is
questions.explanation: Planning sets objectives and decides in advance how to achieve them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Recruiting, training and promoting workers is the management function of
questions.explanation: Staffing (personnel management) fills positions with suitable people and develops them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A sales manager guides, motivates and supervises her sales representatives daily. She is performing the function of
questions.explanation: Directing involves leadership, motivation, communication and supervision.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The production, sales and finance departments of a firm work to different timetables, causing delays. The management function most needed is
questions.explanation: Coordination harmonises the activities of different departments toward common goals.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In an organisation with a line structure, authority flows
questions.A: from the workers up to the managing director
questions.B: directly from the top downwards through each level
questions.D: from outside consultants to the managers
questions.explanation: Line organisation has a clear chain of command from superior to subordinate.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company employs a legal adviser and an HR specialist who advise line managers but do not command them. These positions are
questions.explanation: Staff officers advise and support; line managers have direct authority over operations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The number of subordinates a manager can effectively supervise is called
questions.explanation: A wide span means many subordinates per manager; a narrow span means few.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A worker receives conflicting instructions from two different bosses. The management principle violated is
questions.explanation: Unity of command (Fayol) says each employee should receive orders from one superior only.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A manager gives a supervisor the authority to approve staff leave but remains answerable for the results. This is
questions.explanation: Delegation passes authority downwards; responsibility to the higher level remains.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Board of Directors of a company is elected by
questions.D: the shareholders at the annual general meeting
questions.explanation: Shareholders elect directors to run the company on their behalf.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The top management of a company is responsible for
questions.A: operating the machines on the factory floor
questions.explanation: Top management (board, MD) sets strategy; middle and lower management implement it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An organisation chart shows
questions.A: the prices at which the firm sells each of its products
questions.B: the profit or loss made by each department of the firm in a year
questions.C: the formal structure of positions and lines of authority in the firm
questions.D: the route taken by the firm's goods from the factory to customers
questions.explanation: The chart pictures departments, positions and who reports to whom.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In a functional organisational structure, the firm is divided according to
questions.A: the political opinions held by the firm's senior managers
questions.B: the geographical regions in which the firm sells its products
questions.C: the ages and years of service of the firm's employees
questions.D: specialised activities such as production, marketing and finance
questions.explanation: Functional departments group similar activities under specialist managers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Motivation of workers can be improved by
questions.A: reducing wages while increasing the hours of work
questions.B: fair pay, recognition and opportunities for promotion
questions.C: ignoring every suggestion made by the workers
questions.D: punishing all mistakes severely without explanation
questions.explanation: Both financial and non-financial incentives raise workers' morale and productivity.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A budget is used as a tool of
questions.A: advertising, by informing customers about products
questions.B: staffing, by recruiting and training new workers
questions.C: control, by comparing planned figures with actual results
questions.D: insurance, by covering the firm against fire and theft
questions.explanation: Budgetary control measures performance against the budget and corrects deviations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The management function of organising involves
questions.A: advertising the company's products to consumers
questions.B: setting the goals of the business for the next five years
questions.C: checking actual output against the standards set
questions.D: grouping activities, assigning duties and establishing authority relationships
questions.explanation: Organising builds the structure through which plans are carried out.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a middle-management position?
questions.explanation: Middle managers (departmental or branch managers) link top management and supervisors.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Decentralisation in a large company means that
questions.A: the company operates without any formal organisational structure
questions.B: all decisions are taken at the head office by the managing director
questions.C: decision-making authority is spread to branch and departmental managers
questions.D: the company has been taken over and is now owned by the government
questions.explanation: Decentralisation pushes decisions down to those closest to the operations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A firm sets a standard of 500 units per day, records actual output of 420 and investigates the shortfall. This sequence illustrates
questions.explanation: Control involves setting standards, measuring performance and correcting deviations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The person who represents the interests of the workers in negotiations with management is usually
questions.explanation: Trade unions negotiate wages and conditions on behalf of their members.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Before launching a new noodle brand, a company interviews consumers about their tastes, prices they would pay and where they shop. This activity is
questions.explanation: Market research gathers information about consumers and competitors to guide marketing decisions.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The marketing concept holds that a business should
questions.B: produce as much as possible and force it on the market
questions.C: sell only what the factory finds easy to make
questions.D: identify and satisfy customers' needs profitably
questions.explanation: Marketing starts with the customer's needs rather than with the product.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A soft-drink company sells the same drink in glass bottles, PET bottles and cans at different prices to reach different groups of buyers. It is practising
questions.explanation: Segmentation divides the market into groups with different needs and serves each with a suitable offer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The four Ps of the marketing mix are
questions.explanation: The marketing mix combines product, price, place (distribution) and promotion.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company launches a new smartphone at a very high price aimed at buyers who want the latest model, then lowers the price months later. This pricing strategy is
questions.explanation: Skimming charges a high initial price to recover costs from eager buyers before reducing it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer adds 30% to the cost of every item to arrive at the selling price. This method is
questions.explanation: Cost-plus pricing adds a fixed percentage margin to cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Sales of a brand of cassette players have fallen steadily for years and the company withdraws the product. In the product life cycle the product was at
questions.explanation: In decline, sales and profits fall because of new technology or changing tastes.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In the introduction stage of the product life cycle, a firm usually
questions.A: faces the largest number of competitors
questions.B: earns its highest profits with little promotion
questions.C: withdraws the product from the market
questions.D: spends heavily on promotion while sales are low and profits negative
questions.explanation: At launch the product must be made known; costs are high and sales are just beginning.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A distinctive name, sign or symbol that identifies a firm's product and distinguishes it from competitors' is
questions.explanation: Branding builds recognition and loyalty.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Packaging serves marketing by
questions.A: reducing the need to transport the product to the shops
questions.B: increasing the weight of the product so it sells for more
questions.C: protecting the product and attracting the buyer's attention
questions.D: replacing the need for a brand name on the product
questions.explanation: Good packaging protects, informs and promotes.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company sends sales representatives to visit pharmacies and explain the benefits of a new drug. This element of promotion is
questions.explanation: Personal selling is face-to-face persuasion by sales staff.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A newspaper publishes a favourable report about a company's new factory without the company paying for it. This is
questions.explanation: Publicity is unpaid media coverage; advertising is paid for.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: 'Place' in the marketing mix refers to
questions.A: the office in which the marketing manager and his staff work
questions.B: the factory or workshop in which the goods are manufactured
questions.C: the channels and locations through which the product reaches consumers
questions.D: the country from which the raw materials for the product come
questions.explanation: Place (distribution) covers wholesalers, retailers, transport and outlets.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company sets its price slightly below that of the market leader to win customers. This is
questions.explanation: Competitive (going-rate) pricing is based on rivals' prices rather than on cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Pricing a product at ₦999 instead of ₦1,000 is an example of
questions.explanation: The price seems noticeably lower to the buyer although the difference is trivial.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: After-sales service such as free repairs during the first year helps a firm to
questions.B: reduce the quality of the product
questions.explanation: Service after purchase reassures buyers and encourages repeat business.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A product's warranty (guarantee) is
questions.A: the shop or outlet from which the consumer bought the product
questions.B: the price that the consumer agrees to pay for the product at the time of the sale
questions.C: the brand name and trademark printed on the product and its packaging
questions.D: the seller's promise to repair or replace the product if it proves defective within a period
questions.explanation: Warranties reduce the buyer's risk and signal confidence in quality.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Test marketing means
questions.A: examining samples of the product in the laboratory to detect defects before it is sold
questions.B: introducing a new product in a small area to gauge consumer reaction before a full launch
questions.C: selling old stock at reduced prices in order to clear the shelves for new goods
questions.D: advertising a new product on every radio and television station at the same time
questions.explanation: Test marketing limits the risk of a costly nationwide failure.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The functions of marketing include all of the following EXCEPT
questions.C: manufacturing the product in the factory
questions.explanation: Marketing moves goods from producer to consumer; manufacturing is production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A firm decides to sell its product only to hotels and restaurants rather than to households. This decision concerns its
questions.explanation: The target market is the specific group of customers a firm chooses to serve.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of sales promotion?
questions.A: a television commercial for a bank
questions.B: a 'buy one, get one free' offer on detergent
questions.C: a newspaper article praising a company
questions.D: a salesman's visit to a customer
questions.explanation: Sales promotion uses short-term incentives such as free gifts, coupons and price-offs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Product differentiation means
questions.A: producing goods without a brand name
questions.B: selling exactly the same product as competitors at the same price
questions.C: making a product appear different from competing products through design, quality or branding
questions.D: withdrawing a product from the market
questions.explanation: Differentiation gives buyers a reason to prefer one brand over another.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An advertisement that describes the features of a new phone and its price is
questions.explanation: Informative advertising tells consumers what a product is and where and at what price it is available.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An advertisement urging consumers to 'drink Milkco because it is what strong families drink' is chiefly
questions.explanation: Persuasive advertising appeals to emotions and desires to influence the buyer's choice.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An association of poultry farmers advertises 'Eat more eggs' without naming any brand. This is
questions.explanation: Generic advertising promotes a product class rather than a particular brand.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A small trader wanting to advertise a used car for sale at low cost should use
questions.D: a classified advertisement in a newspaper
questions.explanation: Classified ads are short, cheap and grouped by category.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company that wants to demonstrate how its product works to a mass audience should advertise on
questions.explanation: Television combines sight, sound and motion, making demonstration possible.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which advertising medium is most suitable for reaching farmers in villages where literacy is low and electricity is unreliable?
questions.explanation: Radio is cheap, battery-powered and does not require the audience to read.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Posters placed at the shop entrance and displays beside the goods on the shelves are examples of
questions.explanation: Point-of-sale (point-of-purchase) advertising influences the buyer at the moment of purchase.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An advertising agency is a firm that
questions.A: plans, designs and places advertisements on behalf of clients
questions.C: sells goods to consumers in a shop
questions.D: regulates all advertisements in the country
questions.explanation: Agencies create campaigns and buy media space or time for their clients.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The body that regulates advertising practice in Nigeria and approves advertisements before exposure is
questions.A: the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON)
questions.explanation: ARCON (formerly APCON) vets advertisements and enforces the advertising code.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A disadvantage of advertising to the consumer is that
questions.A: it may create artificial wants and raise the price of goods
questions.B: it informs him about new products
questions.C: it widens his choice of goods
questions.D: it lowers the cost of production through mass sales
questions.explanation: Critics argue advertising costs are passed to consumers and that it encourages unnecessary spending.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Advertising benefits producers mainly by
questions.A: increasing sales, which allows large-scale production and lower unit costs
questions.B: reducing the quantity of goods that they are able to sell in the market
questions.C: eliminating all their competitors from the market within a short time
questions.D: removing the need to maintain good quality in the goods they produce
questions.explanation: Advertising builds demand, enabling economies of scale.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trade journal read by engineers is the most suitable medium for advertising
questions.explanation: Specialised goods are best advertised in media read by the specific buyers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Advertisements sent by post or e-mail directly to selected individuals are called
questions.explanation: Direct mail targets chosen customers with letters, catalogues or e-mails.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company advertises that its battery 'lasts twice as long as the leading brand'. This is
questions.explanation: Competitive advertising compares a brand with rivals to win their customers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following statements about advertising is TRUE?
questions.A: it is a paid form of non-personal communication about products or ideas
questions.B: it is always free of charge to the advertiser
questions.C: it involves face-to-face selling by sales staff
questions.D: it is used only by manufacturers, never by service firms
questions.explanation: Advertising is paid, impersonal communication through mass media by an identified sponsor.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bank advertises its history and contribution to the community rather than any particular product. This is
questions.explanation: Institutional advertising builds the image and goodwill of the organisation as a whole.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Social media advertising on platforms such as Facebook and Instagram is attractive to small businesses because
questions.A: it is relatively cheap and can be targeted at specific groups of users
questions.B: it reaches only people who cannot read newspapers or magazines
questions.C: it requires no internet connection on the part of the audience
questions.D: it is the only advertising medium approved by law for small firms
questions.explanation: Online adverts can be aimed at users by age, location and interests at low cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Misleading advertising is discouraged by law mainly to
questions.A: protect consumers from being deceived into buying unsuitable goods
questions.B: reduce the profits earned by advertising agencies and the media
questions.C: increase the number of billboards along the roads in the cities
questions.D: prevent producers from advertising their goods in any medium
questions.explanation: The advertising code requires claims to be truthful and verifiable.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The agency responsible for registering and regulating foods, drugs and cosmetics in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control registers products and removes unsafe ones.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader sells a bag of cement weighing 40 kg instead of the stated 50 kg. The consumer protection measure violated concerns
questions.explanation: Weights and measures legislation ensures that quantities sold match what is stated.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mrs Ojo bought a generator described as new but found that it had been used. Under the Sale of Goods law, the seller has breached the implied condition that goods must
questions.C: be paid for in cash on delivery
questions.explanation: Goods sold by description must match that description; used goods sold as new breach this condition.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Goods are said to be of 'merchantable quality' when they
questions.A: are fit for the ordinary purpose for which such goods are bought
questions.B: are the cheapest of their kind available in the market
questions.C: have been advertised on television and radio for a month
questions.D: have been imported from a well-known manufacturer abroad
questions.explanation: Merchantable quality is an implied condition in every sale by a trader.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a way in which consumers protect themselves?
questions.A: forming consumer associations and reading labels carefully
questions.B: refusing to buy any goods that are sold in packages
questions.C: buying only the most expensive brands in every shop
questions.D: avoiding shops that issue receipts for goods sold
questions.explanation: Consumer associations, careful buying and insisting on receipts and warranties help consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) protects consumers by
questions.A: investigating complaints, banning unfair practices and enforcing product recalls
questions.B: manufacturing goods of high quality and selling them directly to consumers
questions.C: fixing the prices of all goods and services sold in the markets
questions.D: printing the naira notes that consumers use to pay for goods and services
questions.explanation: The FCCPC enforces the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The NIS mark on a locally made electric cable indicates that
questions.A: the product meets the Nigerian Industrial Standard set by SON
questions.B: the product was imported from Europe
questions.C: the product is exempt from tax
questions.D: the product has been registered by NAFDAC
questions.explanation: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria certifies products that meet its standards.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A consumer who is sold an expired drug should report the seller to
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates drugs and can prosecute sellers of expired or fake medicines.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Government protects consumers by price control when it
questions.A: fixes maximum prices for essential goods such as petrol
questions.B: allows sellers to charge whatever they like
questions.C: bans the sale of all imported goods
questions.explanation: Maximum price legislation prevents exploitation on essential commodities.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A label on food showing ingredients, weight, expiry date and manufacturer's address protects consumers by
questions.A: giving them information to make informed choices
questions.B: increasing the price of the food
questions.C: guaranteeing that the food is free
questions.explanation: Labelling requirements ensure consumers know what they are buying.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Consumer Protection Council was replaced in 2019 by
questions.A: the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
questions.B: the Standards Organisation of Nigeria and its state offices
questions.C: the Nigerian Communications Commission and its zonal offices
questions.D: the National Insurance Commission and its complaints bureau
questions.explanation: The FCCPC took over consumer protection and added competition regulation.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following practices is unfair to consumers?
questions.A: hoarding goods to create artificial scarcity and raise prices
questions.B: issuing receipts to customers for all the goods sold to them
questions.C: displaying the prices of goods clearly on the shelves
questions.D: giving refunds to customers who return defective goods
questions.explanation: Hoarding, adulteration, short-measuring and false advertising exploit consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A caveat emptor ('let the buyer beware') approach has been reduced in modern law because
questions.A: consumers cannot detect defects in complex modern goods before buying
questions.B: sellers in modern markets no longer sell any goods that are defective
questions.C: all goods are now sold by the government at controlled prices
questions.D: consumers are now richer than sellers and can afford any loss
questions.explanation: Implied conditions and consumer agencies shift more responsibility to sellers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Consumer education helps buyers to
questions.A: know their rights and make wise buying decisions
questions.B: produce all the goods they need in their own homes
questions.C: obtain goods from shops free of charge on demand
questions.D: avoid paying value added tax on the goods they buy
questions.explanation: Informed consumers are less likely to be cheated.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A tomato paste manufacturer recalls a batch after discovering contamination and informs the public through the media. This action protects consumers by
questions.A: removing unsafe products from the market before they cause harm
questions.B: raising the price of the remaining stock
questions.C: preventing competitors from selling tomato paste
questions.explanation: Product recall is a consumer protection measure required by law when goods are found unsafe.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Nigerian Communications Commission protects telephone users by
questions.A: regulating tariffs and service quality and handling complaints against operators
questions.B: manufacturing mobile phones and selling them cheaply to subscribers
questions.C: printing recharge cards and distributing them free to subscribers
questions.D: building roads and bridges to the sites of telecommunication masts
questions.explanation: NCC ensures operators meet quality standards and treat subscribers fairly.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trade association is
questions.A: a voluntary body of firms in the same line of business formed to protect their common interests
questions.B: a government agency set up to collect taxes and duties from firms engaged in trade
questions.C: an association of workers in an industry formed to negotiate wages and conditions
questions.D: a company whose shares are bought and sold by investors on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Trade associations (e.g. of bakers or transporters) set standards, lobby and share information.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Unlike a trade union, a trade association represents
questions.A: employers or firms rather than workers
questions.explanation: Trade unions protect employees; trade associations protect businesses in an industry.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Kano Chamber of Commerce has bankers, textile traders, transporters and manufacturers among its members, while the Association of Bakers has only bakeries. The chamber of commerce therefore
questions.A: brings together businesses of all kinds in a locality
questions.B: consists only of firms engaged in one particular trade
questions.C: is owned and financed by the federal government
questions.D: deals only with matters affecting foreign trade
questions.explanation: Chambers of commerce embrace all trades in an area; trade associations are single-industry bodies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a function of a chamber of commerce?
questions.A: organising trade fairs and exhibitions to promote members' businesses
questions.B: fixing the wages and salaries of workers employed in member firms
questions.C: issuing currency notes and coins to members for their transactions
questions.D: collecting customs duty on behalf of the government at the ports
questions.explanation: Chambers organise trade fairs, advise government and issue certificates of origin.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The umbrella body of chambers of commerce, industry, mines and agriculture in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture is the national apex body.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Nigeria Employers' Consultative Association (NECA) represents
questions.A: employers in dealings with the government and trade unions on labour matters
questions.B: workers in wage negotiations with their employers and the government
questions.C: consumers in their complaints against manufacturers and retailers
questions.D: foreign investors seeking licences and permits from the government
questions.explanation: NECA is the voice of employers on labour and employment issues.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trade association helps its members by
questions.A: providing information on markets, standards and government policies
questions.B: paying the salaries of the workers employed by member firms
questions.C: guaranteeing the bank loans taken by member firms
questions.D: buying all the goods produced by member firms at fixed prices
questions.explanation: Information, training, standards and lobbying are core services of trade associations.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trade association may act against the public interest when it
questions.A: fixes prices among members and restricts competition
questions.B: sets quality standards for members' products
questions.D: publishes market statistics for the industry
questions.explanation: Price fixing by an association amounts to a cartel, which competition law forbids.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Members of a trade association finance its activities mainly through
questions.explanation: Members pay annual dues and special levies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A road transport workers' union is different from an association of road haulage companies because the union
questions.A: represents the drivers and workers, while the association represents the company owners
questions.B: represents the owners, while the association represents the drivers
questions.C: is a government agency, while the association is private
questions.D: deals only with foreign trade, while the association deals with home trade
questions.explanation: Unions protect workers; employers' or trade associations protect the firms.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Chambers of commerce assist exporters by
questions.A: issuing certificates of origin and providing information about foreign markets
questions.B: fixing the rate at which the naira exchanges for foreign currencies
