questions.C: collecting export duties from exporters on behalf of the government
questions.D: manufacturing the goods that the exporters sell to foreign buyers
questions.explanation: Chambers certify the origin of goods and connect members with foreign buyers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A chamber of commerce advises the government on
questions.A: policies affecting business, such as taxation and import duties
questions.B: the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
questions.C: the wages to be paid to civil servants
questions.D: the choice of the national football coach
questions.explanation: Chambers lobby government on behalf of the business community.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A new fashion designer must register her business name before opening a shop. She should approach
questions.explanation: CAC registers business names and companies under the Companies and Allied Matters Act.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The government subsidises fertiliser for farmers. The effect on farmers is that
questions.C: they must export all their crops
questions.D: they can no longer sell to wholesalers
questions.explanation: A subsidy is a payment that lowers the price paid by producers or consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The government reduces the import duty on industrial machinery but raises it on finished textiles. The purpose is to
questions.A: encourage local manufacturing and protect local textile producers
questions.B: discourage all industrial activity in the country
questions.C: increase the import of finished textiles
questions.D: reduce employment in the textile industry
questions.explanation: Cheaper machinery helps local industry; higher duty on finished goods protects it from foreign competition.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The government provides roads, electricity and ports for business. These are examples of
questions.explanation: Infrastructure is the basic physical framework on which business depends.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company pays 30% of its profit to the federal government. This tax is
questions.explanation: Companies pay company income tax on profits; VAT is on consumption.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Value added tax (VAT) in Nigeria is
questions.A: a tax on the consumption of goods and services, collected at each stage of sale
questions.B: a tax on the profits made by companies registered in the country
questions.C: a tax deducted from the salaries and wages of workers every month
questions.D: a tax on the ownership of land and buildings in the towns and cities
questions.explanation: VAT is charged on the value added at each stage and borne finally by the consumer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Bank of Industry, SMEDAN and the Industrial Training Fund are all examples of
questions.A: government agencies that support business development
questions.B: trade associations financed by their members
questions.D: commercial banks owned by private shareholders
questions.explanation: These bodies provide finance, training and advisory support to enterprises.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) exists to
questions.A: promote and support small and medium-scale businesses
questions.B: collect taxes from large companies on behalf of the government
questions.C: regulate the stock exchange and protect investors
questions.D: operate the national airline and the federal airports
questions.explanation: SMEDAN provides training, information and access to finance for SMEs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Government regulates business by requiring companies to file annual returns and audited accounts. The main purpose is to
questions.A: protect shareholders, creditors and the public through disclosure
questions.B: increase the profits that the companies make from their business
questions.C: prevent the companies from employing more workers than they need
questions.D: make it impossible for new companies to be formed and registered
questions.explanation: Disclosure lets investors and creditors judge a company's position.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A patent granted by the government gives an inventor
questions.A: the exclusive right to make and sell his invention for a period
questions.B: a free factory to produce the invention
questions.D: a monopoly on all products in his industry
questions.explanation: Patents protect inventions; trademarks protect brands; copyright protects creative works.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company that copies another firm's registered brand name on its products has infringed
questions.explanation: Registered trademarks protect names, logos and symbols that identify goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An author's exclusive right to reproduce and sell her book is protected by
questions.explanation: Copyright covers literary, musical and artistic works.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The government fixes a minimum wage that all employers must pay. This is an example of government
questions.explanation: Labour laws (minimum wage, safety, hours) regulate the relationship between employers and workers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Government participates directly in business when it
questions.A: owns and operates enterprises such as refineries and railways
questions.B: collects taxes and levies from privately owned firms
questions.C: registers companies and business names at the CAC
questions.D: fixes the minimum wage that employers must pay workers
questions.explanation: Direct participation means state ownership through public corporations and government companies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A free trade zone such as the Lekki Free Zone attracts investors by
questions.A: offering tax holidays, duty-free imports of machinery and simplified regulations
questions.B: banning all exports from the zone to other parts of the country
questions.C: requiring investors to pay double the normal rate of company tax
questions.D: forbidding the investors from employing any Nigerian workers
questions.explanation: Free zones offer incentives to attract export-oriented investment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission (NIPC) is responsible for
questions.A: encouraging and registering foreign and local investment in Nigeria
questions.B: regulating advertising practice and approving advertisements
questions.C: supervising insurance companies and brokers in Nigeria
questions.D: operating the seaports and collecting harbour dues
questions.explanation: NIPC promotes investment and grants incentives such as pioneer status.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: 'Pioneer status' granted to a new industry means that the company
questions.A: is exempted from company income tax for a number of years
questions.B: must pay tax at a higher rate than others
questions.C: is owned by the federal government
questions.explanation: Pioneer status is a tax holiday given to industries the government wishes to encourage.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a reason for government regulation of business?
questions.A: to protect consumers, workers and the environment
questions.B: to ensure that all businesses make losses
questions.C: to prevent the formation of new businesses
questions.explanation: Regulation corrects abuses that an unregulated market would allow.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An environmental regulation requires factories to treat their waste before discharging it into rivers. The effect on a factory is to
questions.A: raise its costs but protect the community from pollution
questions.B: reduce its costs and increase pollution
questions.D: guarantee it a higher price for its products
questions.explanation: Pollution controls impose costs on firms in return for social benefits.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) is responsible for
questions.A: collecting federal taxes such as company income tax and VAT
questions.B: registering companies and business names in Nigeria
questions.C: regulating the capital market and protecting investors
questions.D: supervising commercial banks and other financial institutions
questions.explanation: FIRS assesses and collects taxes due to the federal government.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Nigerian government's 'ease of doing business' reforms aim to
questions.A: reduce the time and cost of registering and running a business
questions.B: increase the number of licences a business must obtain
questions.D: close the ports to imported machinery
questions.explanation: Simpler registration, online services and fewer approvals encourage enterprise.
